title: Frac-Fluid Lab
subtitle: Fracturing-fluid lab data, analysed in the browser

card: I built a free lab tool
Paste rheometer readings. Get the analysis.
scenes.text: From rheometer readings to fracture geometry, in one browser tab.
Power-law, Herschel–Bulkley and Carreau fits, each with 95% confidence intervals. Best model chosen by AICc.
Viscosity retention, decay rate during the hold and flow activation energy.
G′ and G″ from oscillation: crossover, relaxation time and a Maxwell fit.
Settling velocity in a non-Newtonian gel, with hindered settling at your proppant loading.
Break kinetics, time to break and residue after breaking.
PKN and KGD: fracture length, width and fluid efficiency, with Carter leak-off.
Ring correction, spinning drop, CMC and Gibbs surface excess.
Compare your gel with a published paper, metric by metric.
Every test comes with a step-by-step lab protocol.
Feedback from lab and field engineers is welcome.
